'''Mehmet Burak Erdoğan''' (born 1972) is a Turkish mathematician, scientist, and professor of mathematics. He is a member of the [[University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign]] (UIUC) Mathematics Department.<ref  name="prwpg">[https://berdogan.web.illinois.edu/ Burak Erdoğan's professional web page in UIUC.]</ref>

==Education==
Burak Erdoğan was born in 1972. He attended the high school Kayseri Fen Lisesi in [[Kayseri]], [[Turkey]], for two years before moving to [[İzmir]], Turkey where he finished the high school Atatürk Lisesi in 1989. He ranked third in the country-wide university entrance exams. He graduated from [[Bilkent University]] Electrical and Electronics Engineering in [[Ankara]] in 1994. He finished his MSc degree in Mathematics department of the same university under the supervision of [[Iossif Ostrovskii|Iossif Vladimirovich Ostrovskii]] in 1996. He received his PhD in Mathematics under the supervision of [[Thomas Wolff]] at [[Caltech]] in 2001.<ref name="gene">[https://www.mathgenealogy.org/id.php?id=11949 Wolff's Record in the Genealogy Project]</ref> He was the last PhD student of Wolff, who died in the last year of Erdoğan's PhD work.<ref>[https://www.ams.org/notices/200105/fea-wolff.pdf A ''Notices'' article on Wolff's legacy]</ref>

==Academic career==
He was a postdoc at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] between 2001-2002 and a visiting assistant professor at [[University of California, Berkeley]] between 2002-2004. Since then he is a faculty member in UIUC Mathematics Department.

He has been an active researcher, having published more than 50 scientific manuscripts with more than 800 citations. He raised 6 PhD students.<ref name="prwpg"/><ref>[https://www.mathgenealogy.org/id.php?id=55896 Burak Erdoğan's Record in the Genealogy Project]</ref>

==Research areas==
His research interests include [[harmonic analysis]] and [[dispersive partial differential equation]]s.
